# Mesh Workbench

> MIT-licensed Blender Python and JSON CLI for coordinate-driven 3D modeling, polygon editing, procedural assemblies, surface patterns and measured local patch reconstruction.

Runs locally inside separately installed Blender. This is not an MCP server or hosted inference service. Source and contributions: https://github.com/shakystar/mesh-workbench

## Start here

- [Agent quickstart](https://shakystar.github.io/mesh-workbench/docs/AGENT_QUICKSTART.md): prerequisites, CLI commands, outputs and failure handling.
- [Operations](https://shakystar.github.io/mesh-workbench/docs/reference/OPERATIONS.md): Python and JSON operation definitions.
- [Status](https://shakystar.github.io/mesh-workbench/docs/STATUS.md): tested versions and current limits.
- [Tool manifest](https://shakystar.github.io/mesh-workbench/tool-manifest.json): descriptive CLI metadata, not an installation protocol.
- [Examples](https://github.com/shakystar/mesh-workbench/tree/main/examples): self-contained procedural recipes.
- [Drill study](https://shakystar.github.io/mesh-workbench/docs/studies/DRILL_SURFACE_STUDY.md): native before/after images and measured evidence.
- [Contributing](https://shakystar.github.io/mesh-workbench/CONTRIBUTING.md): development and pull request workflow.
- [Licensing scope](https://shakystar.github.io/mesh-workbench/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md): original MIT code and separately licensed Blender dependencies.
